Event.title: [Recovered] System load is high for host Victors-MacBook-Pro.local
Event.text:
%%%
## 🚨 What’s happening

High 1-minute load average detected on host Victors-MacBook-Pro.local.

This alert means the system has more processes waiting to run than it can efficiently handle. A high load average often indicates that the host is under significant resource pressure — typically due to CPU saturation, blocked I/O, or memory contention. While some load is normal, consistently high load (especially relative to the number of CPU cores) can signal an unhealthy or overloaded system.

---

## 📈 Impact

If load remains high, the host may experience:

- Slower system and application performance
- Backlogged scheduled jobs or delayed processing
- Increased risk of timeouts, dropped requests, or service degradation

In environments with strict performance requirements, high load can quickly lead to cascading failures or degraded user experience.

---

## 🛠 How to fix (Runbook)

### 🔍 Initial troubleshooting

1. Identify the affected host from the alert.
2. Open [**Infrastructure > Host Details**](https://app.datadoghq.com/infrastructure) for Victors-MacBook-Pro.local.
3. In the **Metrics tab**, examine:
   - `system.load.1`
   - `system.cpu.user`, `system.cpu.system`, `system.io.await`, `system.mem.pct_usable`
4. Use [**Live Processes**](https://app.datadoghq.com/process) to find CPU- or I/O-heavy processes.
5. SSH into the host and run:
   ```bash
   uptime
   top -o %CPU
   
### Cause and Resolution

Cause | Resolution
------|------
CPU-bound processes: | Restart or optimize heavy applications
------|------
Blocked I/O or memory pressure | Investigate disk or memory bottlenecks
------|------
Concurrent workload spikes | Throttle or redistribute jobs across hosts
------|------
Configuration changes | Roll back recent updates or autoscaling settings if related

Event.title: [Recovered] System load is high for host Victors-MacBook-Pro.local
Event.text:
%%%
## 🚨 What’s happening

High 1-minute load average detected on host Victors-MacBook-Pro.local.

This alert means the system has more processes waiting to run than it can efficiently handle. A high load average often indicates that the host is under significant resource pressure — typically due to CPU saturation, blocked I/O, or memory contention. While some load is normal, consistently high load (especially relative to the number of CPU cores) can signal an unhealthy or overloaded system.

---

## 📈 Impact

If load remains high, the host may experience:

- Slower system and application performance
- Backlogged scheduled jobs or delayed processing
- Increased risk of timeouts, dropped requests, or service degradation

In environments with strict performance requirements, high load can quickly lead to cascading failures or degraded user experience.

---

## 🛠 How to fix (Runbook)

### 🔍 Initial troubleshooting

1. Identify the affected host from the alert.
2. Open [**Infrastructure > Host Details**](https://app.datadoghq.com/infrastructure) for Victors-MacBook-Pro.local.
3. In the **Metrics tab**, examine:
   - `system.load.1`
   - `system.cpu.user`, `system.cpu.system`, `system.io.await`, `system.mem.pct_usable`
4. Use [**Live Processes**](https://app.datadoghq.com/process) to find CPU- or I/O-heavy processes.
5. SSH into the host and run:
   ```bash
   uptime
   top -o %CPU
   
### Cause and Resolution

Cause | Resolution
------|------
CPU-bound processes: | Restart or optimize heavy applications
------|------
Blocked I/O or memory pressure | Investigate disk or memory bottlenecks
------|------
Concurrent workload spikes | Throttle or redistribute jobs across hosts
------|------
Configuration changes | Roll back recent updates or autoscaling settings if related

## 🚨 What’s happening

High 1-minute load average detected on host Victors-MacBook-Pro.local.

This alert means the system has more processes waiting to run than it can efficiently handle. A high load average often indicates that the host is under significant resource pressure — typically due to CPU saturation, blocked I/O, or memory contention. ---

## 📈 Impact

If load remains high, the host may experience:

- Slower system and application performance
- Backlogged scheduled jobs or delayed processing
- Increased risk of timeouts, dropped requests, or service degradation

In environments with strict performance requirements, high load can quickly lead to cascading failures or degraded user experience.

---

Cause | Resolution

------|------

Event.text:
%%%
## 🚨 What's happening

Low available memory detected on host Victors-MacBook-Pro.local.

This means the host has less than **10% usable memory** on average over the last 5 minutes, based on the `system.mem.pct_usable` metric. This typically indicates that applications or services are consuming most of the RAM, leaving little room for new processes or memory-intensive operations.

***

## 📈 Impact

If memory remains low, it can lead to:

-   **Slower application performance** due to increased paging or swapping
-   **Crashes or restarts** of services that can’t allocate enough memory
-   **System instability** or degraded responsiveness under load
-   **Failure of background jobs** or scheduled tasks

This may impact key services running on the host and disrupt user-facing or backend operations.

***

## Runbook

### Initial Troubleshooting Steps

1.  **Identify the affected host** from the alert.

2.  Open [**Infrastructure > Host Details**](https://app.datadoghq.com/infrastructure) in Datadog.

3.  In the **Metrics** tab, examine:

    -   `system.mem.pct_usable`, `system.mem.total`, `system.mem.used`
    -   `process.mem.rss`, `process.mem.real`, or specific memory-hungry processes

4.  Use [**Live Processes**](https://app.datadoghq.com/process) to check which processes are using the most memory.

5.  SSH into the host and run:

    ```
    bash
    CopyEdit
    top -o %MEM
    ```

***

### Cause and Resolution

| Cause                                      | Resolution                                                |
| ------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| Memory leaks or runaway processes          | Restart or stop problematic processes                     |
| Memory-intensive workloads                 | Scale up memory capacity or move workloads to other nodes |
| Background jobs or batch tasks overlapping | Stagger or reschedule heavy memory consumers              |
| Misconfigured applications or JVMs         | Tune memory settings (e.g., heap size, buffers)           |

## 🚨 What’s happening

High 1-minute load average detected on host Victors-MacBook-Pro.local.

This alert means the system has more processes waiting to run than it can efficiently handle. A high load average often indicates that the host is under significant resource pressure — typically due to CPU saturation, blocked I/O, or memory contention. While some load is normal, consistently high load (especially relative to the number of CPU cores) can signal an unhealthy or overloaded system.

---

## 📈 Impact

If load remains high, the host may experience:

- Slower system and application performance
- Backlogged scheduled jobs or delayed processing
- Increased risk of timeouts, dropped requests, or service degradation

In environments with strict performance requirements, high load can quickly lead to cascading failures or degraded user experience.

---

## 🛠 How to fix (Runbook)

### 🔍 Initial troubleshooting

1. Identify the affected host from the alert.
2. Open [**Infrastructure > Host Details**](https://app.datadoghq.com/infrastructure) for Victors-MacBook-Pro.local.
3. In the **Metrics tab**, examine:
   - `system.load.1`
   - `system.cpu.user`, `system.cpu.system`, `system.io.await`, `system.mem.pct_usable`
4. Use [**Live Processes**](https://app.datadoghq.com/process) to find CPU- or I/O-heavy processes.
5. SSH into the host and run:
   ```bash
   uptime
   top -o %CPU
   
### Cause and Resolution

Cause | Resolution
------|------
CPU-bound processes: | Restart or optimize heavy applications

Blocked I/O or memory pressure | Investigate disk or memory bottlenecks
------|------

## 🚨 What’s happening

High 1-minute load average detected on host Victors-MacBook-Pro.local.

This alert means the system has more processes waiting to run than it can efficiently handle. A high load average often indicates that the host is under significant resource pressure — typically due to CPU saturation, blocked I/O, or memory contention. While some load is normal, consistently high load (especially relative to the number of CPU cores) can signal an unhealthy or overloaded system.

---

## 📈 Impact

If load remains high, the host may experience:

- Slower system and application performance
- Backlogged scheduled jobs or delayed processing
- Increased risk of timeouts, dropped requests, or service degradation

In environments with strict performance requirements, high load can quickly lead to cascading failures or degraded user experience.

---

### 🔍 Initial troubleshooting

   ```bash

   top -o %CPU

Cause | Resolution
------|------

------|------

This alert means the system has more processes waiting to run than it can efficiently handle. ---

## 📈 Impact

If load remains high, the host may experience:

- Slower system and application performance
- Backlogged scheduled jobs or delayed processing
- Increased risk of timeouts, dropped requests, or service degradation

In environments with strict performance requirements, high load can quickly lead to cascading failures or degraded user experience.

---

This alert means the system has more processes waiting to run than it can efficiently handle. A high load average often indicates that the host is under significant resource pressure — typically due to CPU saturation, blocked I/O, or memory contention. ---

## 📈 Impact

If load remains high, the host may experience:

- Slower system and application performance
- Backlogged scheduled jobs or delayed processing
- Increased risk of timeouts, dropped requests, or service degradation

In environments with strict performance requirements, high load can quickly lead to cascading failures or degraded user experience.

---

   ```bash

events.title: [Recovered] System load is high for host Victors-MacBook-Pro.local
events.text:
%%%
## 🚨 What’s happening

High 1-minute load average detected on host Victors-MacBook-Pro.local.

This alert means the system has more processes waiting to run than it can efficiently handle. A high load average often indicates that the host is under significant resource pressure — typically due to CPU saturation, blocked I/O, or memory contention. While some load is normal, consistently high load (especially relative to the number of CPU cores) can signal an unhealthy or overloaded system.

---

## 📈 Impact

If load remains high, the host may experience:

- Slower system and application performance
- Backlogged scheduled jobs or delayed processing
- Increased risk of timeouts, dropped requests, or service degradation

In environments with strict performance requirements, high load can quickly lead to cascading failures or degraded user experience.

---

## 🛠 How to fix (Runbook)

### 🔍 Initial troubleshooting

1. Identify the affected host from the alert.
2. Open [**Infrastructure > Host Details**](https://app.datadoghq.com/infrastructure) for Victors-MacBook-Pro.local.
3. In the **Metrics tab**, examine:
   - `system.load.1`

## 🚨 What’s happening

High 1-minute load average detected on host Victors-MacBook-Pro.local.

This alert means the system has more processes waiting to run than it can efficiently handle. A high load average often indicates that the host is under significant resource pressure — typically due to CPU saturation, blocked I/O, or memory contention. While some load is normal, consistently high load (especially relative to the number of CPU cores) can signal an unhealthy or overloaded system.

---

## 📈 Impact

If load remains high, the host may experience:

- Slower system and application performance
- Backlogged scheduled jobs or delayed processing
- Increased risk of timeouts, dropped requests, or service degradation

In environments with strict performance requirements, high load can quickly lead to cascading failures or degraded user experience.

---

events.text:
%%%
## 🚨 What’s happening

High 1-minute load average detected on host Victors-MacBook-Pro.local.

This alert means the system has more processes waiting to run than it can efficiently handle. A high load average often indicates that the host is under significant resource pressure — typically due to CPU saturation, blocked I/O, or memory contention. While some load is normal, consistently high load (especially relative to the number of CPU cores) can signal an unhealthy or overloaded system.

---

## 📈 Impact

If load remains high, the host may experience:

- Slower system and application performance
- Backlogged scheduled jobs or delayed processing
- Increased risk of timeouts, dropped requests, or service degradation

In environments with strict performance requirements, high load can quickly lead to cascading failures or degraded user experience.

---

## 🛠 How to fix (Runbook)

### 🔍 Initial troubleshooting

1. Identify the affected host from the alert.
2. Open [**Infrastructure > Host Details**](https://app.datadoghq.com/infrastructure) for Victors-MacBook-Pro.local.
3. In the **Metrics tab**, examine:
   - `system.load.1`
   - `system.cpu.user`, `system.cpu.system`, `system.io.await`, `system.mem.pct_usable`
4. Use [**Live Processes**](https://app.datadoghq.com/process) to find CPU- or I/O-heavy processes.
5. SSH into the host and run:
   ```bash
   uptime
   top -o %CPU
   
### Cause and Resolution

Cause | Resolution
------|------
CPU-bound processes: | Restart or optimize heavy applications
------|------
Blocked I/O or memory pressure | Investigate disk or memory bottlenecks
------|------
Concurrent workload spikes | Throttle or redistribute jobs across hosts
------|------
Configuration changes | Roll back recent updates or autoscaling settings if related

events.text:
%%%
## 🚨 What's happening

Low available memory detected on host Victors-MacBook-Pro.local.

This means the host has less than **10% usable memory** on average over the last 5 minutes, based on the `system.mem.pct_usable` metric. This typically indicates that applications or services are consuming most of the RAM, leaving little room for new processes or memory-intensive operations.

***

## 📈 Impact

If memory remains low, it can lead to:

-   **Slower application performance** due to increased paging or swapping
-   **Crashes or restarts** of services that can’t allocate enough memory
-   **System instability** or degraded responsiveness under load
-   **Failure of background jobs** or scheduled tasks

This may impact key services running on the host and disrupt user-facing or backend operations.

***

## Runbook

### Initial Troubleshooting Steps

1.  **Identify the affected host** from the alert.

2.  Open [**Infrastructure > Host Details**](https://app.datadoghq.com/infrastructure) in Datadog.

3.  In the **Metrics** tab, examine:

    -   `system.mem.pct_usable`, `system.mem.total`, `system.mem.used`
    -   `process.mem.rss`, `process.mem.real`, or specific memory-hungry processes

4.  Use [**Live Processes**](https://app.datadoghq.com/process) to check which processes are using the most memory.

5.  SSH into the host and run:

    ```
    bash
    CopyEdit
    top -o %MEM
    ```

***

### Cause and Resolution

| Cause                                      | Resolution                                                |
| ------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| Memory leaks or runaway processes          | Restart or stop problematic processes                     |
| Memory-intensive workloads                 | Scale up memory capacity or move workloads to other nodes |
| Background jobs or batch tasks overlapping | Stagger or reschedule heavy memory consumers              |
| Misconfigured applications or JVMs         | Tune memory settings (e.g., heap size, buffers)           |

events.text:
%%%
## 🚨 What's happening

Low available memory detected on host Victors-MacBook-Pro.local.

This means the host has less than **10% usable memory** on average over the last 5 minutes, based on the `system.mem.pct_usable` metric. This typically indicates that applications or services are consuming most of the RAM, leaving little room for new processes or memory-intensive operations.

***

## 📈 Impact

If memory remains low, it can lead to:

-   **Slower application performance** due to increased paging or swapping
-   **Crashes or restarts** of services that can’t allocate enough memory
-   **System instability** or degraded responsiveness under load
-   **Failure of background jobs** or scheduled tasks

This may impact key services running on the host and disrupt user-facing or backend operations.

***

## Runbook

### Initial Troubleshooting Steps

1.  **Identify the affected host** from the alert.

2.  Open [**Infrastructure > Host Details**](https://app.datadoghq.com/infrastructure) in Datadog.

3.  In the **Metrics** tab, examine:

    -   `system.mem.pct_usable`, `system.mem.total`, `system.mem.used`
    -   `process.mem.rss`, `process.mem.real`, or specific memory-hungry processes

4.  Use [**Live Processes**](https://app.datadoghq.com/process) to check which processes are using the most memory.

5.  SSH into the host and run:

    ```
    bash
    CopyEdit
    top -o %MEM
    ```

***

### Cause and Resolution

| Cause                                      | Resolution                                                |
| ------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| Memory leaks or runaway processes          | Restart or stop problematic processes                     |
| Memory-intensive workloads                 | Scale up memory capacity or move workloads to other nodes |
| Background jobs or batch tasks overlapping | Stagger or reschedule heavy memory consumers              |
| Misconfigured applications or JVMs         | Tune memory settings (e.g., heap size, buffers)           |

## 🚨 What’s happening

High 1-minute load average detected on host Victors-MacBook-Pro.local.

This alert means the system has more processes waiting to run than it can efficiently handle. A high load average often indicates that the host is under significant resource pressure — typically due to CPU saturation, blocked I/O, or memory contention. While some load is normal, consistently high load (especially relative to the number of CPU cores) can signal an unhealthy or overloaded system.

---

## 📈 Impact

If load remains high, the host may experience:

- Slower system and application performance
- Backlogged scheduled jobs or delayed processing
- Increased risk of timeouts, dropped requests, or service degradation

In environments with strict performance requirements, high load can quickly lead to cascading failures or degraded user experience.

---

## 🛠 How to fix (Runbook)

### 🔍 Initial troubleshooting

1. Identify the affected host from the alert.

- Slower system and application performance

- Increased risk of timeouts, dropped requests, or service degradation

High 1-minute load average detected on host Victors-MacBook-Pro.local.

This alert means the system has more processes waiting to run than it can efficiently handle. A high load average often indicates that the host is under significant resource pressure — typically due to CPU saturation, blocked I/O, or memory contention. While some load is normal, consistently high load (especially relative to the number of CPU cores) can signal an unhealthy or overloaded system.

---

## 📈 Impact

If load remains high, the host may experience:

- Slower system and application performance
- Backlogged scheduled jobs or delayed processing
- Increased risk of timeouts, dropped requests, or service degradation

In environments with strict performance requirements, high load can quickly lead to cascading failures or degraded user experience.

---

Cause | Resolution

## 🚨 What’s happening

High 1-minute load average detected on host Victors-MacBook-Pro.local.

This alert means the system has more processes waiting to run than it can efficiently handle. A high load average often indicates that the host is under significant resource pressure — typically due to CPU saturation, blocked I/O, or memory contention. While some load is normal, consistently high load (especially relative to the number of CPU cores) can signal an unhealthy or overloaded system.

---

## 📈 Impact

If load remains high, the host may experience:

- Slower system and application performance
- Backlogged scheduled jobs or delayed processing
- Increased risk of timeouts, dropped requests, or service degradation

In environments with strict performance requirements, high load can quickly lead to cascading failures or degraded user experience.

---

Cause | Resolution

## 🚨 What’s happening

High 1-minute load average detected on host Victors-MacBook-Pro.local.

This alert means the system has more processes waiting to run than it can efficiently handle. A high load average often indicates that the host is under significant resource pressure — typically due to CPU saturation, blocked I/O, or memory contention. While some load is normal, consistently high load (especially relative to the number of CPU cores) can signal an unhealthy or overloaded system.

---

## 📈 Impact

If load remains high, the host may experience:

- Slower system and application performance
- Backlogged scheduled jobs or delayed processing
- Increased risk of timeouts, dropped requests, or service degradation

In environments with strict performance requirements, high load can quickly lead to cascading failures or degraded user experience.

---

## 🛠 How to fix (Runbook)

### 🔍 Initial troubleshooting

1. Identify the affected host from the alert.
2. Open [**Infrastructure > Host Details**](https://app.datadoghq.com/infrastructure) for Victors-MacBook-Pro.local.
3. In the **Metrics tab**, examine:
   - `system.load.1`
   - `system.cpu.user`, `system.cpu.system`, `system.io.await`, `system.mem.pct_usable`
4. Use [**Live Processes**](https://app.datadoghq.com/process) to find CPU- or I/O-heavy processes.
5. SSH into the host and run:
   ```bash
   uptime
   top -o %CPU
   
### Cause and Resolution

Cause | Resolution
------|------
CPU-bound processes: | Restart or optimize heavy applications
------|------
Blocked I/O or memory pressure | Investigate disk or memory bottlenecks
------|------
Concurrent workload spikes | Throttle or redistribute jobs across hosts
------|------
Configuration changes | Roll back recent updates or autoscaling settings if related
